execution.description: First run of the remote-setup transport library: ssh-docker and ssh-container behind one interface and one record, the container's fixed scripts run in real bash starting the real job server as a process, and the Challenge-neutral remote_gpu route driven by a synthetic second Challenge.

expected: Every transport test passes on the first run, the container scripts start and stop a real job server process, and the route modules name no Challenge.
observed: One failure on the first run: the Challenge-neutral grep test found the word battery in a remote_runner docstring example; rewording fixed it. Formatting through scripts/dev/canonical.sh did not persist, because its non-interactive mode runs on a copy of the checkout. ruff format and black disagreed on a parenthesized one-string tuple member; black is the gate check_quality enforces.
keep: A grep test that the route modules name no Challenge catches a literal in prose as well as in code.

Container scripts are tested as real bash with only a container's tools on PATH, and the worker's Python is a wrapper over this interpreter, so the real job server runs as a real process with setsid and is found again by its environment marker.
A synthetic second Challenge (a ChallengeCampaign registered nowhere) is the proof that a route takes the Challenge as a parameter.
change: Format in place with the native venv (.venv/bin/python -m black) and use canonical.sh only to verify: ruff check, black --check, check_quality --base origin/main and check_diff_hygiene.
Write a refusal's next step as one string that fits a line, so ruff format and black agree.
